findings.text: The commit removes the guard that skipped package families whose original roots have different case modes. Trusted and candidate directories with the same spelling now merge again across mixed case modes, and `migration_check/prepare.py` uses this merged view for export and replay, so owner review required. There is also a trap in this path: when the workspace volume ignores case and only one original root does, the merged `Model` directory also answers lookups for `model`. Those lookups then resolve to the first root's files, but in the original search path the case-sensitive root would not supply them. Fix: have the owner review the restored grouping across mixed modes, and decide whether the merged view must also be checked against the workspace's own case mode.

The docstring says different spellings combine "only when all roots ignore case", but the code checks only the roots that contain that package family (`modes` is keyed per casefolded family). So a reader can think that one unrelated case-sensitive root turns off alias merging for every package. Fix: change the text to "only when every original root that contains that package ignores case".
